findings.claim: Filtering empty expr now happens before interpolation, so a target whose expr is only a variable that resolves to '' (e.g. '$query' with an empty textbox) survives into the shard path. It is grouped into otherQueries, and runSplitQuery then drops it, leaving requests=[]. runSplitGroupedQueries does Math.max(...[]) and requests.filter(...)[0].partition, which throws inside a .then(). That is an unhandled rejection: the Observable never emits or completes, the panel spins forever, and valid sharded queries in the same request never run.
findings.evidence: Commit 76ffba5f6d reordered the steps to filter then applyTemplateVariables (shardQuerySplitting.ts:50-52). Trace: groupTargetsByQueryType (shardQuerySplitting.ts:244-251) -> runSplitQuery (shardQuerySplitting.ts:163) -> querySplitting.ts:298 filter -> runSplitGroupedQueries querySplitting.ts:95-96 with no empty guard. Reasoned, not run. Proposed red test: targets [{refId:'A',expr:'sum(count_over_time({a="b"}[1m]))'},{refId:'B',expr:'$empty'}], replace maps '$empty' to '', fetchLabelValues resolves ['1','2']; expect runShardSplitQuery to emit and runQuery to have been called. On HEAD it times out. The standards seat separately noted that empty-after-interpolation targets are no longer dropped.
findings.reason: Plausible hang regression with a concrete trace and a stated red test. The cheapest fix is to filter on expr after the applyTemplateVariables map (or guard runSplitGroupedQueries against empty requests). Must be made red before fixing.

findings.claim: Ad-hoc filters (and template interpolation) are now applied more than once per query: twice on the time-split path (runSplitQuery, then DataSourceWithBackend.query) and three times on the shard path (runShardSplitQuery, runSplitQuery, super.query). Before the patch it was once. Filters added after a parser are appended without a duplicate check, so the LogQL sent to Loki grows to '| k=`v` | k=`v` [| k=`v`]', and split and non-split paths send different query text.
findings.evidence: DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185 calls applyTemplateVariables(q, scopedVars, filters) again. Sub-requests are {...request, targets}, so filters carry through. shardQuerySplitting.ts:52 and :163 re-enter runSplitQuery. modifyQuery.ts:494 dedupes only stream-selector labels (labelExists). addFilterAsLabelFilter (modifyQuery.ts:510-541) always appends, and the existing modifyQuery.test.ts:46 case shows the append. The old shard path used interpolateVariablesInQueries with no filters. The 5-call assertion at shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:112 confirms the repeated interpolation passes. Reasoned, not run. Proposed red test: a real createLokiDatasource with filters [{key:'k',operator:'=',value:'v'}] and expr 'rate({a="b"} | logfmt [5m])'; assert that the runQuery target is a fixed point of applyTemplateVariables. Seat severities split: Important (superpowers, mattpocock), Minor (open-code-review, ponytail). All seats agree results are unchanged because the filters are idempotent.
findings.reason: Kept at Important because a correctness seat rated it so and it changes the executed LogQL relative to base and to the non-split path. Fix by interpolating into local copies used only for classification and step grouping (or by not passing filters), and by not re-interpolating inside runSplitQuery when it is called from the shard path. Same root cause at shardQuerySplitting.ts:52.

findings.claim: expect(applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5) pins an internal call count (1 shard call plus 4 sub-requests). It locks in the redundant re-interpolation and breaks on any behaviour-preserving refactor.
findings.evidence: shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:110-112. The toHaveBeenCalledWith/runQuery payload assertion that follows already covers the contract.
findings.reason: Tests an implementation detail and will block the fix for the ad-hoc double-application finding. Drop the assertion.

findings.claim: The new 'Interpolates queries before execution' tests (here and at shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:84) mock templateSrv.replace to expand $__auto to 5m. Production applyTemplateVariables strips __auto from scopedVars, so $__auto reaches the backend unexpanded. The [5m] assertions test the mock; only the step assertion reflects real behaviour.
findings.evidence: datasource.ts:1113 removes __auto from scopedVars in applyTemplateVariables. The test mock replaces on every call.
findings.reason: The test asserts behaviour production never produces. Make the mock honour scopedVars removal or assert only on step and user variables.

findings.claim: No test covers request.filters (ad-hoc filters) or the $__range no-split guard on the new interpolation path. Both new tests pass no filters and use plain string-replace mocks.
findings.evidence: querySplitting.test.ts:75-88 and shardQuerySplitting.test.ts:84-101 build requests without filters.
findings.reason: This is the missing guard for the ad-hoc double-application finding; its red test doubles as this coverage.

findings.claim: Running templateSrv.replace again on already-interpolated text is not idempotent: a variable value containing a literal $name that matches another defined variable gets expanded again on each later pass (twice on the split path, three times on the shard path).
findings.evidence: Same repeated applyTemplateVariables passes as the ad-hoc finding (querySplitting.ts:299, shardQuerySplitting.ts:52, DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185). Reasoned. The ponytail seat judged it an edge case not worth a fix.
findings.reason: ponytail: rare edge case (variable values containing $identifier). It disappears as a side effect if the ad-hoc double-application fix removes the repeated interpolation; recheck after that fix.

findings.claim: The shard path now leaves $__auto/$__interval/$__range for the backend (resolved per time-split chunk) instead of resolving them client-side via interpolateVariablesInQueries. This is an unannounced user-visible behaviour change; the shard-values selector also now includes ad-hoc stream matchers.
findings.reason: Not a defect. The raising seat itself says it matches the non-shard path and is not a bug. open-code-review independently notes that it makes the querySupportsSplitting $__range guard work on the shard path. It is a behaviour alignment, not a regression.

findings.claim: Duplicated tests: 'Interpolates queries before execution' appears in both test files, and shardQuerySplitting.test.ts has a near-duplicate pair at lines 84 and 110.
findings.reason: The raising seat labels it a baseline code smell with no documented standard behind it, and the override block excludes generic smells. The ponytail seat found the cross-file copies justified because they cover two separate public entry points. The line-110 assertion problem is handled by the call-count finding.
